convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load 'Modified_Optimum_Elliptic_Filter' which is an unknown custom indicator, plus includes external TradeAlgorithms.mqh library for order management. Custom indicator logic cannot be auto-replicated without the indicator source code.

derived_values.name: Value[0..2] - three consecutive buffer 0 readings from Modified_Optimum_Elliptic_Filter starting at SignalBar
derived_values.formula: CopyBuffer(handle, 0, SignalBar, 3, Value) → Value[0]=bar(SignalBar+2), Value[1]=bar(SignalBar+1), Value[2]=bar(SignalBar)

other_exits: Long position closed when filter value rises (Value[1] > Value[2] triggers BUY_Close if BuyPosClose=true)
Short position closed when filter value falls (Value[1] < Value[2] triggers SELL_Close if SellPosClose=true)

custom_logic_notes: Signal logic: Reads 3 consecutive values from custom indicator buffer 0 at offset SignalBar. Entry requires two conditions: (1) directional bias from Value[1] vs Value[2] comparison, and (2) continuation confirmation from Value[0] vs Value[1]. When Value[1]<Value[2] (filter declining), a long entry is triggered if Value[0]>Value[1] (filter turning up = reversal confirmation). When Value[1]>Value[2] (filter rising), a short entry is triggered if Value[0]<Value[1] (filter turning down = reversal confirmation). This is essentially a zero-lag filter turning-point detection strategy. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose input booleans gate each action independently. GlobalVariableDel_ cleanup on deinit via TradeAlgorithms.mqh. SignalBar=1 means signals are read from the previous completed bar (not current bar), making this a proper close-of-bar strategy.
external_dependencies: Modified_Optimum_Elliptic_Filter.ind (custom indicator file required at runtime)
python_conversion_notes: The custom indicator 'Modified_Optimum_Elliptic_Filter' must be reimplemented in Python or its formula obtained before backtesting is possible. The Elliptic Filter is a digital signal processing filter — look for the indicator source in the same MQL5 download package. Once the indicator is replicated, the signal logic is straightforward: compare 3 consecutive filter values for turning-point detection. Entry: BUY when filter[1]<filter[2] AND filter[0]>filter[1]; SELL when filter[1]>filter[2] AND filter[0]<filter[1]. Exit via opposing signal, SL=1000 points, TP=2000 points. Position sizing uses margin-based lot calculation (MM=0.1, mode=LOT). The TradeAlgorithms.mqh helper functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, CIsNewBar, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory) need Python equivalents — standard backtrader/zipline patterns will suffice.
